acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Orcs family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Warchief, T4, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Skull-Totem Line Commander (Champion) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two earth construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Towering and thick as a door, with iron-capped tusks, plate over fur, one greataxe in each hand, and a skull totem rising from a harness across the broad back.

Signature mechanic: Totem Turn: the Warchief rotates the skull totem toward one arena quarter, causing Grunts to shoulder-test inward, Warriors to breach across them, and Berserkers to begin Bloodbeat along the painted boundary; the Warchief then locks both greataxes into a slow crossing guard that cannot pivot away from that quarter.
battlefieldDuty: Plant and rotate a clan front around a skull totem, ordering committed attacks into complementary lanes while guarding the command point with paired greataxes.
constructionDimensions: Equipment takes on quarry-built weight through slate lamellae, basalt axe cheeks, rawhide stone cradles, ocher mineral paint, and clan totems set into cracked load-bearing plinths.
Stance and locomotion become braced and fault-driven: wider planted feet, dragged stone counterweights, dust compression, and visible fracture lines show where mass is anchored before it releases.
counterplay: Move against the indicated rotation, bait the fixed crossing guard into empty space, then cut the totem lashings from the rear; without it, lower forms resume local tells and no longer cover one another's recoveries. Affinity signal: Pale fault lines spread from a planted boot through the loaded weapon or totem; striking the marked joint after the committed release breaks the brace and exposes the trailing side.
forbiddenTreatments: Palette-only earth treatment without mineral load paths, bracing, and fracture behavior
Glow-only earth treatment without stone construction or a readable fault signal
Pasted rocks that hide the top-heavy Orc silhouette
Seamless stone bodies that erase skin, scars, tusks, leather, and iron
identityInvariants: Tall, broad, top-heavy humanoid silhouette with a thick neck, wide shoulders, heavy jaw, forward lean, and lower tusks rising past the lip.
Gray-green or ash-gray skin is framed by blood red, black, dark iron, bone white, and readable red or white war paint.
Boiled leather, fur, riveted iron, bone, and crude steel remain thick, weighty, and practical rather than elegant or finely matched.
Scars, paint, tusk rings, piercings, skull trophies, spiked pauldrons, and clan totems communicate earned encounter rank without becoming a biological claim.
Tusk length, muscle mass, posture, and carried trophies escalate together, but every form retains committed heavy motion and exposed recovery as the family combat grammar.
telegraph: The gate-sized iron rings on its tusks strike together, the skull totem tips toward a painted quarter, and every nearby Orc turns its marked shoulder or scar lattice along the same boundary.
